1#main: Who is believed regarding inflicting a blemish on a firstborn. In it are 11 seifim. Kohanim are suspected of inflicting a blemish on a firstborn—even if he is a sage sitting in the study hall. If he did something that appears deceptive, such as giving the firstborn barley in a basket in a manner that when it comes to eat them it damages its lip, or the like—they do not slaughter based on that blemish. (Therefore any blemish fit to come by human action—they do not slaughter based on it until witnesses testify it befell on its own (Tur).)
2#main: All blemishes fit to come by human action—a shepherd is believed to say they fell on their own and were not made intentionally, and they slaughter based on them. In what case is this said? When the shepherd was an Israelite and the firstborn is in the kohen's hand; but if the shepherd was a kohen and the firstborn is still in the Israelite owner's hand—he is not believed, and they suspect him lest he inflicted it in order to receive it. (And some say a kohen shepherd is believed regarding an Israelite's firstborn, and one may be lenient (Tur in the name of the Rosh and Ramban).)
3#main: A kohen who testified for another kohen that this blemish fell on its own—is believed, and they are not concerned lest they do favors for one another.
4#main: Even his sons and household members testify for him about the firstborn; but not his wife, because she is like his own body.
5#main: Until he testified from the mouth of another witness that this blemish fell unintentionally—he is believed; even a woman is believed to say, "In my presence this blemish fell on its own," and they slaughter based on it.
6#main: If it was not presumed that it is a firstborn, and the kohen said, "This is a firstborn and this blemish befell it on its own"—he is believed.
7#main: A firstborn that was in a kohen's hand and a blemish befell it, and one witness testified about it that this blemish fell on its own—and we do not know if this blemish is one for which they slaughter the firstborn—and the kohen in whose hand it is said, "I showed this blemish [to an expert] and they permitted slaughter"—he is believed, and they are not concerned lest he did not show it.
8#main: And likewise a kohen is believed to say about a blemished firstborn, "This Israelite gave it to me in its blemished state," and they are not concerned lest he inflicted it—for a matter done openly, people do not lie about it.
9#main: An Israelite is believed to say, "I gave this firstborn to the kohen in its blemished state," even if it was a lamb and it grew large, and they are not concerned lest he does not recognize it.
10#main: Israelites are not suspected regarding firstborns—even their own; therefore an Israelite who has doubt whether a firstborn was eaten in its blemished state by the owners is believed to say a blemish befell it on its own.
11#main: They do not show the firstborn to an Israelite until a kohen is with him, lest the expert say it is a blemish and permitted to slaughter, and he go slaughter it for himself and not give it to the kohen—for although he is not suspected of eating consecrated food outside, he is suspected of stealing priestly gifts; therefore if he was a sage known to be scrupulous, they show it to him (and likewise if) the blemish was open to all, such as if its hand or foot was cut off—since he brought it to the expert sage, he is presumed scrupulous; therefore they show it to him even though no kohen is with him.
